question.prompt: A boat has a speed of \(x\) kilometers per hour in still water, and the current has a speed of 3 kilometers per hour. Traveling 48 kilometers downstream takes the same amount of time as traveling 36 kilometers upstream. Find \(x\).

solutions.explanation: Set up the equation \(\frac{48}{x+3}=\frac{36}{x-3}\). Clearing the denominators gives \(48(x-3)=36(x+3)\), so \(x=21\). Checking confirms that it fits the practical situation.
solutions.title: Equate downstream and upstream times

solutions.explanation: The downstream and upstream speeds are \(x+3\) and \(x-3\), with \(x>3\) for upstream travel. Their difference is \(3+3=6\) kilometers per hour. Over equal durations, this produces the distance difference \(48-36=12\) kilometers, so the common duration is \(12\div6=2\) hours. The downstream speed is therefore \(48\div2=24\) kilometers per hour, giving \(x=24-3=21\) kilometers per hour. The upstream speed is then \(18>0\), and \(36\div18=2\) hours as required.
solutions.title: Use the speed and distance differences
